about: The single source of the accountable-passive detector's word lists. scripts/gen-agency-lexicon.mjs writes it into the JavaScript, Python and Go engines between BEGIN and END GENERATED AGENCY LEXICON markers, and its --check (run by test/agency-lexicon.test.mjs) fails when any engine's copy drifts. A mark needs all of: a past passive auxiliary; at most one adverb; a participle from one of the classes; the head word its class names, when it names one; no 'by' in the next byWindow words of the clause; and the participle's requires and unless conditions. The matcher reads an ASCII-lowercased copy of the text, so every word here is lowercase ASCII, and a phrasal participle is written with one space.

classes.why: The participle itself names a fault: someone mishandled, misjudged, neglected or tampered.
The participle names a breach of something held in trust, mostly someone's data.
The participle names a concealment or a withdrawal someone decided on.

classes.head: error
classes.why: A light verb says little alone; after an error, decision or statement noun it is the classic deletion ('mistakes were made', 'steps were taken').

classes.head: challenge
classes.why: 'Concerns were raised' deletes the accuser. After any other noun 'raised' is no deletion: software raises an error ('an error was raised'), and a threat level is raised.

classes.head: dummy
classes.why: Only the impersonal 'it was decided' deletes who decided.

classes.head: data
classes.why: After a data noun, these verbs say the data went to someone else: the act the taxonomy's lesson 'your data was shared' names.

excluded.why: Present, modal and progressive passives ('is executed', 'can be frozen', 'were being withheld') describe procedure or ongoing state far more often than a deleted doer; every held-out false positive of the earlier detector was present or modal.
A get-passive is also an idiom ('got fired up', 'got lost'); the words alone cannot tell them apart.
Harm and news verbs: 'Lives were lost in the earthquake', 'Your account was closed at your request'. The words alone cannot say a doer exists, so the rule marks nothing.

Routine data handling: methods sections, retention notices and transfer logs use them as procedure ('Data were collected from 200 participants.', 'Records were retained for seven years.', 'Data were transferred to a secure server.'). The words alone say no harm, fault or concealment.
